hints.title: Greedy Interval Selection
hints.text: To cover each index while maximizing unused intervals, always pick the interval that extends furthest to the right.

hints.title: Tracking Available Intervals
hints.text: Sort intervals by their start index and push available intervals into a max priority queue by their end index.

hints.title: Difference Array Maintenance
hints.text: Maintain active coverage using a difference array or expiration queue, popping furthest reaches when coverage is insufficient.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```python
import heapq

class Solution:
    def maxRemoval(self, nums: list[int], queries: list[list[int]]) -> int:
        n = len(nums)
        queries.sort(key=lambda q: q[0])
        
        available = []
        diff = [0] * (n + 1)
        curr_coverage = 0
        q_idx = 0
        used = 0
        
        for i in range(n):
            curr_coverage += diff[i]
            while q_idx < len(queries) and queries[q_idx][0] == i:
                heapq.heappush(available, -queries[q_idx][1])
                q_idx += 1
            
            while curr_coverage < nums[i]:
                if not available or -available[0] < i:
                    return -1
                r = -heapq.heappop(available)
                curr_coverage += 1
                diff[r + 1] -= 1
                used += 1
                
        return len(queries) - used
```

complexity.notes: Greedy choice of available interval with furthest right reach using a priority queue.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Exhaustive search of query subsets requires exponential time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Identifies greedy interval selection with priority queue and difference array.
